sentences.en: 33 presidents.
sentences.zh: 33位总统。

sentences.en: I called the president at 4.30 in the morning and he answered.
sentences.zh: 我在清晨4点半给总统打了电话，他接了。

sentences.en: Seven decades in space.
sentences.zh: 在太空中走过七十年。

sentences.en: We want to see what's beyond the next star.
sentences.zh: 我们想看看下一颗星星的背后有什么。

sentences.en: A thousand consumer product guides.
sentences.zh: 一千份消费品指南。

sentences.en: Today I am testing seven mattresses.
sentences.zh: 今天我正在测试七张床垫。

sentences.en: 60 super sundaes.
sentences.zh: 60款超级圣代。

sentences.en: They were probably the best team in the league every single year.
sentences.zh: 他们可能每年都是联赛中最棒的队伍。

sentences.en: 53,500 puzzles.
I use a different starting word every day.
sentences.zh: 我每天都用不同的起始单词。

sentences.en: 25,000 recipes.
And I love a one-pan recipe because I don't love washing pans.
sentences.zh: 而且我很喜欢单锅菜谱，因为我讨厌洗锅。

sentences.en: The New York Times, celebrating 175 years of helping you understand the world and make the most of each day.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》庆祝175周年，陪伴您理解世界，过好每一天。

sentences.en: Subscribe now for a special offer at nytimes.com slash subscribe.
sentences.zh: 立即订阅即可享受特别优惠，网址为 nytimes.com 加上斜杠 subscribe。

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴巴罗，来自《纽约时报》。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这里是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Nearly six decades after the United States put men on the moon.
sentences.zh: 在美国将人类送上月球近六十年后。

sentences.en: That's one small step for men.
sentences.zh: 这是我个人的一小步。

sentences.en: It is returning to that mission.
sentences.zh: 它正在重返这一使命。

sentences.en: And today, a major step in that process will begin in Florida.
sentences.zh: 今天，这一进程中的重要一步将在佛罗里达州拉开帷幕。

sentences.en: My colleague, Ken Chang, is there and explains why it is that the United States wants to go back to the moon.
sentences.zh: 我的同事肯·张正在现场，他将解释为什么美国想要重返月球。

sentences.en: It's Wednesday, April 1St.
sentences.zh: 今天是4月1日，星期三。

sentences.en: Ken, welcome back to The Daily.
sentences.zh: 肯，欢迎再次来到《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Good to be here again.
sentences.zh: 很高兴再次来到这里。

sentences.en: So, we always turn to you when something big and meaningful is happening in space and something big and meaningful is happening today, weather permitting.
sentences.zh: 所以，每当太空发生重大而有意义的事情时，我们总是会找你，而今天，如果天气允许的话，就有一件重大而有意义的事情要发生。

sentences.en: So, does the weather permit this big and meaningful thing to happen on Wednesday?
sentences.zh: 那么，周三的天气允许这件重大而有意义的事情发生吗？

sentences.en: Hopefully, it looks good.
sentences.zh: 希望如此，看起来不错。

sentences.en: The forecast says 80% chance that it's going to go, but that means there's 20% chance that something doesn't quite clear up.
sentences.zh: 天气预报说有80%的几率顺利发射，但这意味著还有20%的几率会有什么状况没完全排除。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Okay, those are pretty good odds.
sentences.zh: 好吧，这胜算相当不错。

sentences.en: So, start by describing this mission.
sentences.zh: 那么，先来介绍一下这次任务吧。

sentences.en: This is the first time that anyone's going close to the moon in more than 53 years.
sentences.zh: 这是53年多来首次有人类飞近月球。

sentences.en: Well, four astronauts are going to be blasting off from Kennedy Space Center in Florida.
sentences.zh: 嗯，四名宇航员将从佛罗里达州的肯尼迪航天中心发射升空。

sentences.en: And they're going to head out to the moon.
sentences.zh: 他们将前往月球。

sentences.en: They're not going to land.
sentences.zh: 他们不会着陆。

sentences.en: They're just going to swing around the moon and then head straight back to Earth and splash down in the Pacific Ocean 10 days later.
sentences.zh: 他们只会绕月飞行，然后直接返回地球，10天后在太平洋溅落。

sentences.en: And why?
sentences.zh: 为什么呢？

sentences.en: I mean, as you've just hinted at, some 50-so years ago, astronauts from the United States did that very thing.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，正如你刚才暗示的那样，大约50年前，美国的宇航员就做过这件事。

sentences.en: So, why are we doing it again?
sentences.zh: 所以，我们为什么又要这样做呢？

sentences.en: So, the goal this time in this program, which is called Artemis, is to get people back to the moon, but also stay there this time.
sentences.zh: 这次被称为“阿尔忒弥斯”计划的目标，是将人类送回月球，但这次还要留在那里。

sentences.en: And so, this program is broken up into pieces because it's really hard to land on the moon.
sentences.zh: 所以这个计划被拆分成了好几个部分，因为在月球着陆真的很难。

sentences.en: And you don't want to do all the hard things all at once.
sentences.zh: 你不会想把所有困难的事情一下子全做了。

sentences.en: You want to break it up into pieces so you do step by step.
sentences.zh: 你希望把它拆分，一步一步来。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So, Artemis 1, back in 2022, it sent this spacecraft to the moon and spent several weeks there, but without any people aboard.
sentences.zh: 所以，在2022年的“阿尔忒弥斯1号”任务中，飞船被发送到了月球并在那里停留了数周，但上面没有任何人。

sentences.en: So, that sort of established that the basic machinery works.
sentences.zh: 这基本上证实了基本机械装置是可以运作的。

sentences.en: Now, we're on the next step, which is Artemis 2.
sentences.zh: 现在，我们进入了下一步，也就是“阿尔忒弥斯2号”。

sentences.en: This time, they're including the four people aboard.
sentences.zh: 这一次，他们将在船上搭载四名宇航员。

sentences.en: And that's critical because the main task of this mission is to test the life support systeMs.
sentences.zh: 这至关重要，因为这次任务的主要任务是测试生命维持系统。

sentences.en: And it's impossible to test it without actual people producing carbon dioxide, producing water and poop and everything else that you need to clean up.
sentences.zh: 如果不让真正的人类产生二氧化碳、产生水、排泄物以及其他所有需要清理的东西，是根本无法测试它的。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So, that's this mission.
sentences.zh: 这就是这次任务。

sentences.en: Step one was, can we get an aircraft around the moon?
sentences.zh: 第一步是，我们能不能把飞行器送到月球周围？

sentences.en: Step two is, can we get people on this craft to live?
sentences.zh: 第二步是，我们能把人送上这艘船并在上面生活吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: The biggest goal for the astronauts on this mission is to not die.
sentences.zh: 这次任务中宇航员最大的目标就是活下来。

sentences.en: And if Artemis 2 succeeds, NASA can move on to the next steps, which will lead to attempts to land astronauts on the moon in a couple years.
sentences.zh: 如果“阿尔忒弥斯2号”成功，美国宇航局就可以推进下一步，这将在几年内引导实现让宇航员在月球着陆的尝试。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: And at this point, I may sound like a broken record, but why?
sentences.zh: 此时此刻，我可能听起来像个复读机，但为什么呢？

sentences.en: I mean, what is the rationale for trying to do this thing that we did with great fanfare
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们当年大张旗鼓地做过这件事

sentences.en: 50-something years ago?
sentences.zh: 50年前，现在这样做的基本理由是什么？

sentences.en: What NASA says is that this time, we're not going to just go there and then forget about it.
sentences.zh: 美国宇航局表示，这一次，我们不会只是去一趟然后把它抛在脑后。

sentences.en: That this will be the first step to building a moon base to—
sentences.zh: 这将是建设月球基地的第一步——

sentences.en: A moon base.
sentences.zh: 一个月球基地。

sentences.en: Yeah, so that they're going to start putting a power plant, some habitats, to allow people to stay there for days, weeks, months.
sentences.zh: 是的，他们将开始建造发电厂、一些居住舱，让人们能在那里停留几天、几周甚至几个月。

sentences.en: So, at first, it will probably be a scientific research station, much like what we have in
sentences.zh: 所以，起初它可能是一个科学研究站，很像我们在

sentences.en: Antarctica near the South Pole.
sentences.zh: 南极洲南极附近建立的基地。

sentences.en: Beyond that, people will start thinking about how we can take advantage of the moon's resources.
sentences.zh: 在此之后，人们将开始思考我们如何利用月球的资源。

sentences.en: They might even start trying to mine valuable materials that could be found there, such as helium-3.
sentences.zh: 他们甚至可能开始尝试开采那里可以找到的宝贵材料，例如氦-3。

sentences.en: And what's helium-3, and why do we want to mine it on the moon?
sentences.zh: 什么是氦-3？为什么我们要在月球上开采它？

sentences.en: So, helium-3 is a light version of helium, and it's quite rare on Earth.
sentences.zh: 氦-3是氦的一种轻同位素，在地球上相当罕见。

sentences.en: It's a little bit more prevalent on the moon's surface.
sentences.zh: 它在月球表面的储量要稍微普遍一些。

sentences.en: And this is a version of helium that could be very useful in future fusion reactors.
sentences.zh: 这是氦的一种版本，在未来的聚变反应堆中非常有用。

sentences.en: It's also thought to be useful for future quantum computers, which people are very excited about because it could be used for artificial intelligence, among other things.
sentences.zh: 人们还认为它对未来的量子计算机很有用，大家对此非常兴奋，因为它可以用于人工智能等领域。

sentences.en: And helium-3 on Earth costs roughly $3 million a pound.
sentences.zh: 地球上的氦-3价格大约是每磅300万美元。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: So, if you can even get a little bit from the moon, you could probably make a profit.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你能从月球上弄回哪怕一点点，你大概就能盈利了。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So, what lies in the future is space research and potentially some serious commercial mining.
sentences.zh: 因此，未来展现在面前的是太空研究，以及潜在的大规模商业采矿。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: They're still speculative, but there are companies who are planning to do things along those lines already.
sentences.zh: 这些仍然带有推测性，但已经有一些公司在计划朝这些方向开展工作了。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: And then there's scientific dreamers who want to do something like build a big radio telescope on the far side of the moon to listen to the universe.
sentences.zh: 然后还有一些科学梦想家，他们想做一些事情，比如在月球背面建造一个大型射电望远镜来倾听宇宙。

sentences.en: Listen to the universe.
sentences.zh: 倾听宇宙。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: There's signals from just after the Big Bang billions of years ago.
sentences.zh: 有来自数十亿年前大爆炸之后的信号。

sentences.en: But it's hard to do that from Earth because we've basically made things very noisy with
sentences.zh: 但从地球很难做到这一点，因为我们基本上通过

sentences.en: TV, cell phone calls, podcasts.
sentences.zh: 电视、手机通话和播客，让周围环境变得非常嘈杂。

sentences.en: But on the far side of the moon, you have the entire thickness of the moon blocking all that noise.
sentences.zh: 但在月球背面，你拥有整个月球的厚度来阻挡所有这些噪音。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: So, you can hear the rest of the universe.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以听到宇宙中其余的声音。

sentences.en: Wait, just so I understand, we can build a giant listening post on the far side of the moon where it's dead quiet, and we could hear the ancient sounds of really the dawn of
sentences.zh: 等等，为了让我理解清楚，我们可以在月球背面建造一个巨大的监听站，那里死一般的寂静，我们可以听到真正可以说是

sentences.en: time itself.
sentences.zh: 时间之初的远古声音。

sentences.en: Pretty much.
sentences.zh: 差不多吧。

sentences.en: These would be almost the echoes of the Big Bang.
sentences.zh: 这些几乎就是大爆炸的回声。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: And the other thing they want to do is use the moon as a testing ground for technologies that they ultimately want to put on Mars.
sentences.zh: 他们想做的另一件事是将月球作为测试技术的试验场，这些技术他们最终想要应用到火星上。

sentences.en: That would include nuclear power plants, habitats, life support systems, because many of the conditions on the moon are things you'll ultimately have to face on Mars as well.
sentences.zh: 这包括核电站、居住舱、生命维持系统，因为月球上的许多条件也是你最终在火星上必须面对的。

sentences.en: So, basically, we'd use the moon and its conditions and its gravity to figure out whether something we eventually want to have on Mars can first survive the moon.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上，我们会利用月球及其环境和引力，来弄清楚我们最终想在火星上拥有的东西是否能首先在月球上存活。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And then there's this romantic notion of humanity just spreading out into the solar system, that we are no longer just confined to one planet, but we can live elsewhere as well,
sentences.zh: 然后还有一种浪漫的想法，即人类向太阳系扩散，我们不再局限于一颗星球，而是也能在其他地方生活，

sentences.en: someday on a moon colony.
sentences.zh: 有朝一日建立月球殖民地。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: But on top of all that, there's also the geopolitical competition with China.
sentences.zh: 但除了所有这些之外，还有与中国的地缘政治竞争。

sentences.en: And, of course, we want to do all this before they do.
sentences.zh: 当然，我们希望在他们之前完成这一切。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: If we are to be a multi-planet species, Americans would like to be the firSt.
sentences.zh: 如果我们注定要成为一个多星球物种，美国人希望成为第一名。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Because the people who are there first are the ones who make the rules of how space commerce
sentences.zh: 因为最先到达那里的人，才是制定太空商业规则的人

sentences.en: is conducted, will have the prime locations on the moon, and control the resources, and so on.
sentences.zh: 将在月球上拥有黄金地段，控制资源，诸如此类。

sentences.en: So, being first means being the one who's in charge.
sentences.zh: 所以，成为第一就意味着成为掌控全局的人。

sentences.en: Ken, what you have just laid out is a tremendous vision for the future, and all of it rests on the
sentences.zh: 肯，你刚刚描绘的是一幅宏伟的未来愿景，而这一切都压在

sentences.en: shoulders of four astronauts who are going to be blasting off toward the moon in a few hours on Wednesday there in Florida.
sentences.zh: 四名宇航员的肩上，他们将在佛罗里达州周三的几个小时后发射升空前往月球。

sentences.en: True.
sentences.zh: 确实。

sentences.en: True.
sentences.zh: 确实。

sentences.en: But that's probably not what is going to be on their minds.
sentences.zh: 但这可能不是他们脑子里在想的事情。

sentences.en: Remember, their first job is staying alive.
sentences.zh: 记住，他们的首要工作是活下来。

sentences.en: If they don't do that, then all these dreams are pushed even farther into the future.
sentences.zh: 如果他们做不到这一点，那么所有这些梦想都会被推到更遥远的未来。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: New York Times games are made by people, like the ones you just heard from.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的游戏是由真人制作的，就像你刚刚听到那些人一样。

sentences.en: Go to nytimes.com slash games to start playing today.
sentences.zh: 访问 nytimes.com 加上斜杠 games 开始今天的游戏。

sentences.en: Ken, can you introduce us to these four astronauts who have all this responsibility on their shoulders
sentences.zh: 肯，你能向我们介绍一下这四位肩负重任的宇航员，

sentences.en: and describe the logistics of this 10-day mission they're embarking on from their perspective?
sentences.zh: 并从他们的角度描述他们即将开始的这趟10天任务的后勤保障吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: The commander is Reed Weissman.
sentences.zh: 指挥官是里德·怀斯曼。

sentences.en: We just need to go execute this mission and bring a little bit of each of our own personalities in.
sentences.zh: 我们只需要去执行这项任务，并带上我们各自的一点个性。

sentences.en: He's a former fighter pilot in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 他是美国海军的前战斗机飞行员。

sentences.en: Navy.
sentences.zh: 他曾在中东执行过两次部署任务。

sentences.en: He served in the Middle East on two deployments.
sentences.zh: 在卸任宇航员办公室主任之前，他一直是该职位的负责人，这使他能够被指派执行登月任务。

sentences.en: And he was the head of the astronaut office before he stepped down, which allowed him to be assigned to the moon mission.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 我昨晚在外面，抬头看着月球心想，下次我看到这个景象时，我们很有可能已经绕过背面并返回了。

sentences.en: I was outside last night, and I was looking up at the moon and thinking, the next time I see this site, there's a good chance that we will have been around the far side and back.
sentences.zh: 关于他还有一个细节。

sentences.en: And there's also a point in detail about him.
sentences.zh: 他的妻子几年前去世了。

sentences.en: His wife died a few years ago.
sentences.zh: 所以他去月球意味着要将女儿们留在身后10天。

sentences.en: So him going to moon means leaving his daughters behind for 10 days.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: Well.
sentences.zh: 所以我希望其中有一部分也能超越载人航天飞行本身。

sentences.en: And so I hope there's a piece of it that extends beyond human spaceflight as well.
sentences.zh: 维克托·格洛弗，他也是前海军飞行员。

sentences.en: Victor Glover, he's also a former naval aviator.
sentences.zh: 十年后，当下一个具有挑战性的事情发生时，也许我们可以回过头来看著这个，说，嘿，大家，还记得我们做过那件事吗？

sentences.en: Ten years from now, when the next challenging thing happens, maybe we can look back on this and go, hey guys, remember we did that?
sentences.zh: 我们有我们自己的登月计划，记得吗？

sentences.en: We had our own moonshot, remember?
sentences.zh: 那是全球性的。

sentences.en: And it was global.
sentences.zh: 那是国际性的。

sentences.en: It was international.
sentences.zh: 而我们一起做到了。

sentences.en: And we did it together.
sentences.zh: 他是第一位在空间站服役并延长停留时间的黑人男性。

sentences.en: He was the first black man to serve and extend his stay on the space station.
sentences.zh: 现在他将成为第一位去月球的黑人男性。

sentences.en: And now he'll be the first black man to go to the moon.
sentences.zh: 接下来是克里斯蒂娜·科赫。

sentences.en: Next is Christina Koch.
sentences.zh: 我们中的任何人都不可能比被要求做的事情更伟大，但我们可以尽到自己的一份力，展现最好的自己，齐心协力完成它。

sentences.en: None of us can be as big as what we're asked to do, but we can contribute the part and bring our best selves and come together to do it.
sentences.zh: 她受过专业训练，是一名电气工程师。

sentences.en: And she's an electrical engineer by training.
sentences.zh: 在被美国宇航局选为宇航员之前，她实际上一直在地面上从事美国宇航局的任务工作。

sentences.en: And she actually worked on NASA missions on the ground before she was selected by NASA to become an astronaut.
sentences.zh: 她现在保持着女性单次太空飞行时间最长的纪录，长达328天。

sentences.en: And she now holds the record for the longest single spaceflight by a woman of 328 days.
sentences.zh: 并且现在她保持着女性单次太空飞行时间最长的纪录，长达328天。

sentences.en: So that's almost a full year.
sentences.zh: 差不多正好是一整年。

sentences.en: All these things that we talk about first are really not about any one individual's accomplishment, but more about celebrating where we are at.
sentences.zh: 我们首先谈论的所有这些事情，其实并不是关于某一个人的成就，而是更多地庆祝我们所处的位置。

sentences.en: And finally, there's Jeremy Hansen.
sentences.zh: 最后，还有杰瑞米·汉森。

sentences.en: He's the Canadian on the crew.
sentences.zh: 他是乘组中的加拿大人。

sentences.en: You can't fix all the problems in the world, but you can influence the little bit around you.
sentences.zh: 你无法解决世界上所有的问题，但你可以对周围的一小部分人产生影响。

sentences.en: It'll be the first time that a non-American has gone to deep space.
sentences.zh: 这将是非美国人第一次进入深空。

sentences.en: We don't know the ripple effects of what we're about to do, but we can do it well to the best of our ability and have joy while we're doing it.
sentences.zh: 我们不知道我们即将做的事情会产生什么样的连锁反应，但我们可以尽我们最大努力把它做好，并在做的过程中享受快乐。

sentences.en: And hopefully that will make a small contribution.
sentences.zh: 希望这能做出微小的贡献。

sentences.en: And he has a sense of humor about this.
sentences.zh: 对此他很有幽默感。

sentences.en: He said, if something goes wrong on this mission, then NASA can blame Canada.
sentences.zh: 他说，如果这次任务出了什么问题，那么NASA就可以责怪加拿大了。

sentences.en: Okay, so that is the crew.
sentences.zh: 好的，这就是乘组人员。

sentences.en: Talk to us about their next 10 days as they're going to experience it, the four of them, together.
sentences.zh: 跟我们聊聊他们接下来的10天，他们四个人将要共同经历的历程。

sentences.en: So they'll have a very long day before launch even.
sentences.zh: 因此，甚至在发射之前，他们就会迎来非常长的一天。

sentences.en: They'll wake up eight hours before launch.
sentences.zh: 他们将在发射前八小时醒来。

sentences.en: They have to get into their spacesuits.
sentences.zh: 他们必须穿上航天服。

sentences.en: They'll be driven out to a launch pad.
sentences.zh: 他们将被用车送到发射台。

sentences.en: They'll go up this huge tower and enter their spacecraft.
sentences.zh: 他们将登上这座巨大的塔楼并进入他们的航天器。

sentences.en: It's known as Orion.
sentences.zh: 它被称为“猎户座”。

sentences.en: Then they'll be sitting there for about four hours until the countdown clock gets to zero.
sentences.zh: 然后他们会在那里坐上大约四个小时，直到倒计时时钟归零。

sentences.en: And eight minutes later, they'll be in space.
sentences.zh: 八分钟后，他们就会进入太空。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: And that first day in space will also be quite busy.
sentences.zh: 太空中的第一天也将相当忙碌。

sentences.en: They won't immediately go to the moon.
sentences.zh: 他们不会立即去月球。

sentences.en: In fact, what they'll do is make two looping orbits around Earth.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他们要做的是绕地球飞行两个环形轨道。

sentences.en: And the reason they're doing that is they want to take this time to check out every little system on the spacecraft to make sure it's working before they make the decision to fire the engines to send them off to the moon.
sentences.zh: 他们这样做的原因是，他们想利用这段时间检查航天器上的每一个小系统，确保它正常工作，然后才做出点燃发动机将他们送往月球的决定。

sentences.en: Basically, a couple of test flights.
sentences.zh: 基本上就是几次试飞。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So after day two, when they fire the engines to head to the moon, the moon is close to a quarter million miles from Earth.
sentences.zh: 所以在第二天，当他们点燃发动机前往月球时，月球距离地球将近二十五万英里。

sentences.en: So it takes a while to get there.
sentences.zh: 所以到达那里需要一段时间。

sentences.en: Basically, four days.
sentences.zh: 基本上是四天。

sentences.en: And they'll be spending all this time in this capsule, which has about as much space as two minivans.
sentences.zh: 他们将把所有时间都花在这个太空舱里，里面的空间大约相当于两辆面包车。

sentences.en: Two minivans.
sentences.zh: 两辆面包车。

sentences.en: And I say this as a father that fills basically a minivan.
sentences.zh: 我作为一个塞满了基本上是一辆面包车东西的父亲来说这句话。

sentences.en: That's not a lot of space.
sentences.zh: 那空间可真不大。

sentences.en: It's actually a little bit more than it'd be on Earth because you get to float around.
sentences.zh: 实际上比在地球上要稍微大一点，因为你可以飘来飘去。

sentences.en: So you can use all the space above you.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以利用你头顶上所有的空间。

sentences.en: It's not quite as crowded as it would be if you were driving cross country.
sentences.zh: 不像如果你开车进行跨国旅行那样拥挤。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So on day six is the big event.
sentences.zh: 所以第六天是大日子。

sentences.en: This is when they're closest to the moon.
sentences.zh: 这是他们距离月球最近的时候。

sentences.en: And they're not super close.
sentences.zh: 而且他们离得并不是超级近。

sentences.en: So the way NASA describes it, the moon will appear about the size of a basketball held at arm's length.
sentences.zh: 按照NASA的描述，月球看起来大约有一只手臂伸直时拿着的篮球那么大。

sentences.en: And the moon's gravity will basically pull them around the moon and they'll go behind the moon.
sentences.zh: 月球的引力基本上会把他们拉着绕过月球，他们会去到月球背面。

sentences.en: And so that means they'll lose all radio communication with Earth for about 40 minutes.
sentences.zh: 这意味着他们将失去与地球的所有无线电通信约40分钟。

sentences.en: And we won't know what's going on until they emerge on the other side.
sentences.zh: 在我们看到他们从另一侧出现之前，我们不会知道发生了什么。

sentences.en: And during this time, they'll also be making all these observations of the far side of the moon.
sentences.zh: 在此期间，他们还将对月球背面进行所有的观测。

sentences.en: Such as?
sentences.zh: 比如什么？

sentences.en: So what's really interesting is that they will be seeing parts of the far side of the moon that no human eyes have seen before.
sentences.zh: 所以非常有趣的是，他们将看到人类以前从未见过的月球背面的部分区域。

sentences.en: And that's because the last time an astronaut passed over the far side of the moon, it was a different time of day.
sentences.zh: 这是因为上次有宇航员从月球背面掠过时，是一天中的不同时间。

sentences.en: And those areas were in darkness.
sentences.zh: 而那些区域当时处于黑暗中。

sentences.en: So that's fascinating.
sentences.zh: 所以这太迷人了。

sentences.en: These astronauts, because there will be light, will cast their eyes on parts of the moon that no human being has ever seen before in actual daylight.
sentences.zh: 这些宇航员，因为会有光线，将把目光投向月球上从未有人在真正日光下亲眼见过的区域。

sentences.en: Correct.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: On the moon, there's no street light.
sentences.zh: 在月球上，没有路灯。

sentences.en: So the last time an astronaut passed over these parts, it was completely dark.
sentences.zh: 所以上次宇航员经过这些区域时，这里是一片漆黑。

sentences.en: So Ken, as these astronauts are moving along the far side of the moon, you had said that the moon's gravity was going to be holding them down.
sentences.zh: 那么，肯，当这些宇航员沿月球背面移动时，你刚才说月球的引力会拉住他们。

sentences.en: How much power will they have to actually direct the craft that they're in during this period?
sentences.zh: 在此期间，他们有多大权力来真正控制他们所在的飞船？

sentences.en: The trajectory that they're on, NASA designed it specifically that they actually don't need to use the engines to bring them back to Earth.
sentences.zh: 他们所在的轨道，NASA专门设计成实际上不需要使用发动机就能把他们带回地球。

sentences.en: But it's going along a path that the gravity of the moon basically is going to sling them around and throw them right back toward Earth without them doing much of anything.
sentences.zh: 但它沿着这样一条路径运行：月球的引力基本上会像投石器一样把他们甩出去，直接把他们抛回地球，而他们不需要做太多事情。

sentences.en: So in a sense, they're kind of powerless to do much themselves.
sentences.zh: 所以在某种意义上，他们自己其实无能为力。

sentences.en: They're at the mercy of the moon's gravitational push and pull.
sentences.zh: 他们只能任由月球引力的推拉摆布。

sentences.en: Which is a good thing because it's much easier to be headed back to Earth than into deep space where who knows where you would end up.
sentences.zh: 这是一件好事，因为返回地球比前往深空要容易得多，谁知道你在深空会最终落到哪里。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So assuming this gravitational slingshot system brings these four astronauts safely home, what happens?
sentences.zh: 所以，假设这个引力弹弓系统把这四名宇航员安全带回家，接下来会发生什么？

sentences.en: So once they complete their lunar flyby, they have to spend another three days just sitting around waiting to get back to Earth.
sentences.zh: 一旦他们完成了绕月飞行，他们还得花另外三天时间闲坐着等待返回地球。

sentences.en: This is probably the boring part of the trip.
sentences.zh: 这可能是旅程中最无聊的部分。

sentences.en: It's, are we there yet?
sentences.zh: 就是那种，“我们到了吗？”的状态。

sentences.en: On the very last day, Earth's gravity is going to be pulling them around Earth, and they'll be on a path to re-enter the atmosphere,
sentences.zh: 在最后一天，地球的引力将把他们拉向地球周围，他们将走上重新进入大气的轨道，

sentences.en: and they'll splash down the Pacific Ocean off San Diego.
sentences.zh: 他们将在圣地亚哥附近的太平洋溅落。

sentences.en: They'll be plucked out of the ocean, taken to a ship, and then flown back to shore where they'll be checked out by doctors.
sentences.zh: 他们将被从海里捞出来，送上一艘船，然后乘飞机回到岸上，在那里接受医生的检查。

sentences.en: And then they'll get to fly back to Houston.
sentences.zh: 然后他们将坐飞机返回休斯顿。

sentences.en: And that will be the end of Artemis II.
sentences.zh: 这将是“阿尔忒弥斯2号”的结束。

sentences.en: And assuming that the astronauts leave this process in tip-top shape, which we, of course, hope they do,
sentences.zh: 假设宇航员们以极佳的状态结束这一过程，我们当然希望他们如此，

sentences.en: my sense is that this is going to be a really proud moment for NASA because from everything I've taken from your reporting in the lead-up to Artemis II,
sentences.zh: 我的感觉是，这将是NASA非常自豪的时刻，因为从我在“阿尔忒弥斯2号”之前的所有报道中了解到的情况来看，

sentences.en: it's really a NASA production through and through and not what we think of when we think of the modern space system where things kind of get divided up between NASA and these well-known private companies,
sentences.zh: 这完全是NASA自始至终一手打造的产品，而不是我们想象中的现代太空系统——事情被分摊给NASA和这些知名私企，

sentences.en: Jeff Bezos, Elon Musk.
sentences.zh: 杰夫·贝佐斯、埃隆·马斯克。

sentences.en: You're right, Michael.
sentences.zh: 你说的对，迈克尔。

sentences.en: This is old-school NASA, where NASA designed and operated their various spacecraft.
sentences.zh: 这是老派的NASA，当时NASA设计并运营他们自己的各种航天器。

sentences.en: And it'll be a triumph for them in that the old ways of doing things succeeded.
sentences.zh: 对他们来说，这将是一场胜利，因为旧的做法成功了。

sentences.en: But on the very next mission, Artemis III, the new space companies, SpaceX, run by Elon Musk, and Blue Origin, started by Jeff Bezos,
sentences.zh: 但在紧接着的下一次任务“阿尔忒弥斯3号”中，由埃隆·马斯克运营的新太空公司SpaceX，以及由杰夫·贝佐斯创立的蓝色起源，

sentences.en: they become involved because SpaceX and Blue Origin are producing the lunar landers that are eventually going to take astronauts to the surface of the moon.
sentences.zh: 他们参与进来了，因为SpaceX和蓝色起源正在制造最终将宇航员带到月球表面的登月舱。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: So in these next phases, these big private companies are going to be providing some of the really key equipment that will allow NASA to land on the moon.
sentences.zh: 所以在接下来的这些阶段中，这些大型私企将提供一些真正关键的设备，让NASA能够登陆月球。

sentences.en: So in that sense, Artemis II is kind of the end of an era?
sentences.zh: 所以从这个意义上说，“阿尔忒弥斯2号”算是一个时代的结束吗？

sentences.en: In a sense, yes.
sentences.zh: 从某种意义上说，是的。

sentences.en: There's an expectation that this will be the last big NASA spacecraft and rockets.
sentences.zh: 人们预计这将是NASA最后的大型航天器和火箭。

sentences.en: And in the future, there will be much more work from private companies like SpaceX and Blue Origin.
sentences.zh: 在未来，将会有更多来自SpaceX和蓝色起源等私营公司的工作。

sentences.en: You know, Ken, just to end this conversation, it's pretty hard to ignore the context of when Artemis II is happening right now.
sentences.zh: 你知道，肯，在结束这次对话之际，几乎很难忽视“阿尔忒弥斯2号”目前发生时的背景。

sentences.en: We're in the middle of a war.
sentences.zh: 我们正处于一场战争之中。

sentences.en: And it's big, and it's controversial, and it has had ripple effects across the entire world.
sentences.zh: 这场战争规模很大，充满争议，并在全世界产生了连锁反应。

sentences.en: And I think of space exploration as, at its best, this big unifying experience for the whole world.
sentences.zh: 我认为太空探索在其最佳状态下，是整个世界的一场伟大的团结体验。

sentences.en: And this mission comes at a moment that's not so unifying.
sentences.zh: 而这次任务正值一个不那么团结的时刻。

sentences.en: But if you think back to the 1960s, when we went to the moon for the first time, that was a turbulent era, especially the year 1968.
sentences.zh: 但如果你回想20世纪60年代我们第一次登上月球的时候，那是一个动荡的时代，尤其是1968年。

sentences.en: Martin Luther King was assassinated.
sentences.zh: 马丁·路德·金遇刺身亡。

sentences.en: Robert Kennedy was assassinated.
sentences.zh: 罗伯特·肯尼迪遇刺身亡。

sentences.en: The country was mired in the Vietnam War.
sentences.zh: 国家陷入越南战争的泥潭。

sentences.en: The Democratic Convention in Chicago was beset by riots.
sentences.zh: 芝加哥的民主党全国代表大会爆发了骚乱。

sentences.en: It was a very unsettled time in the United States.
sentences.zh: 那是美国一个非常动荡的时期。

sentences.en: And at the end of that year, December of 1968...
sentences.zh: 而那年年底，1968年12月……

sentences.en: The engines are armed.
sentences.zh: 发动机已解除保险。

sentences.en: Four, three, two, one, zero.
sentences.zh: 四，三，二，一，零。

sentences.en: We have committed...
sentences.zh: 我们已经点火……

sentences.en: Apollo 8 launch.
sentences.zh: 阿波罗8号发射。

sentences.en: Oh, and there's the rumble in our building.
sentences.zh: 哦，我们大楼都在轰鸣。

sentences.en: And that was the equivalent of Artemis II.
sentences.zh: 这就相当于“阿尔忒弥斯2号”。

sentences.en: It's a beautiful takeoff so far.
sentences.zh: 到目前为止，这是一次美丽的起飞。

sentences.en: It was the first launch of the mighty Saturn V rocket that NASA used then with people aboard.
sentences.zh: 这是NASA当时载人使用的强大的土星五号火箭的首次发射。

sentences.en: And the three astronauts on Apollo 8, they went to the moon, orbited the moon, and on Christmas Eve, as they were in orbit around the moon,
sentences.zh: 阿波罗8号上的三名宇航员飞往月球，环绕月球飞行，在平安夜，当他们处于环月轨道时，

sentences.en: the three astronauts took turns reading Genesis from the Bible.
sentences.zh: 这三名宇航员轮流朗读了《圣经》中的《创世记》。

sentences.en: It was such a calming, hopeful moment that some people even talked about how that mission saved 1968.
sentences.zh: 这是一个如此令人平静、充满希望的时刻，以至于有人甚至讨论那次任务拯救了1968年。

sentences.en: So we don't know what the four astronauts on Artemis II are planning to say as they are coming back from the moon.
sentences.zh: 所以我们不知道“阿尔忒弥斯2号”的四名宇航员在从月球返回时打算说些什么。

sentences.en: But still,
sentences.zh: 但尽管如此，

sentences.en: just the imagery that's going to come back of them seeing Earth from a quarter million miles away could just provide a moment of calm that makes us realize we are still all part of the same planet.
sentences.zh: 仅仅是他们从二十五万英里外看到地球的画面传回，就能带来一刻的平静，让我们意识到我们仍然属于同一个星球。

sentences.en: And perhaps we'll just offer a note of hope that maybe it won't be as turbulent as it seems right now.
sentences.zh: 也许它会带来一丝希望，也许情况不会像现在看起来那么动荡。

sentences.en: Well, Ken, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 好的，肯，非常感谢。

sentences.en: We appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 我们很感激。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: I hope it goes off perfectly later today.
sentences.zh: 我希望今天晚些时候它能完美发射。

sentences.en: Me too.
sentences.zh: 我也是。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天需要了解的其他内容。

sentences.en: On Tuesday afternoon,
sentences.zh: 周二下午，

sentences.en: a federal judge ordered that President Trump end construction of his proposed massive ballroom off the east wing of the White House until the project is blessed by Congress.
sentences.zh: 一名联邦法官下令，要求特朗普总统停止在白宫东翼旁建造他提议的大型宴会厅，直到该项目得到国会批准。

sentences.en: The decision delivered the first meaningful setback to the president's increasingly bold efforts to redesign the White House.
sentences.zh: 这一裁决对总统越来越大胆的白宫重新设计努力造成了第一次实质性挫折。

sentences.en: And for the first time since the start of the war in Iran, the average price of gasoline across the United States surpassed $4 a gallon, a major milestone for consumers.
sentences.zh: 自伊朗战争爆发以来，全美汽油平均价格首次突破每加仑4美元，这对消费者来说是一个重大的里程碑。

sentences.en: I'm not happy about this.
sentences.zh: 我对此很不高兴。

sentences.en: And even my customers are coming in this morning and saying, what happened?
sentences.zh: 甚至我的顾客今天早上也走进来问，发生什么事了？

sentences.en: What happened in 24 hours where we went?
sentences.zh: 怎么在24小时内我们就变成这样了？

sentences.en: In Jacksonville, Florida, Cam Judy, the gas station manager we spoke to for Friday's episode, raised his prices on Tuesday to $4.29 a gallon.
sentences.zh: 在佛罗里达州杰克逊维尔，我们在周五节目中采访过的加油站经理卡姆·朱迪在周二将价格提高到每加仑4.29美元。

sentences.en: That's up more than 50 percent since the start of the war.
sentences.zh: 自战争爆发以来，这一涨幅已超过50%。

sentences.en: And it just caught everybody off guard, including myself.
sentences.zh: 这让所有人都措手不及，包括我自己。

sentences.en: So it's upsetting and I hope it doesn't last long.
sentences.zh: 所以这令人沮丧，我希望这种情况不会持续太久。

sentences.en: Prices are expected to remain high until oil can flow freely through the Strait of Hormuz.
sentences.zh: 预计油价将保持高位，直到石油能够自由通过霍尔木兹海峡。

sentences.en: Today's episode was produced by Alex Stern, Jack DeSidoro, Rochelle Bonja, and Diana Nguyen.
sentences.zh: 今天的节目由亚历克斯·斯特恩、杰克·德西多罗、罗谢尔·邦贾和戴安娜·阮制作。

sentences.en: It was edited by Rachel Quester and contains music by Marian Lozano, Dan Powell, and Diane Wong.
sentences.zh: 由蕾切尔·奎斯特剪辑，包含玛丽安·洛萨诺、丹·鲍威尔和黛安·王创作的音乐。

sentences.en: Our theme music is by Wonderly.
sentences.zh: 我们的主题音乐由旺德利创作。

sentences.en: This episode was engineered by Alyssa Moxley.
sentences.zh: 本期节目由阿丽莎·莫克斯利工程制作。

sentences.en: Special thanks to Timothy Bella.
sentences.zh: 特别感谢蒂莫西·贝拉。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这就是今天的《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直作为一个受严密控制的机器运作。

sentences.en: Until this summer.
sentences.zh: 直到今年夏天。

sentences.en: When elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 当时选举迎来了群自称改革派的人。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，该党一直陷入一场残酷、混乱、有时又令人兴奋的斗争中。

sentences.en: In the latest episode of Metro with me, Sarah Koenig, stories of people trying to maintain their influence and losing control along the way.
sentences.zh: 在我主持的《都市》最新一期中，讲述了人们试图维持其影响力却在过程中失去控制的故事。

sentences.en: Metro.
sentences.zh: 《都市》。

sentences.en: Listen wherever you get your podcasts.
sentences.zh: 请在您获取播客的任何地方收听。

sentences.en: Let's come.
sentences.zh: 来吧。
